messages:
ben (AcmeCorp): Hey support — our org hit 0 credits right before the monthly reset and a bunch of streaming sessions dropped. UI showed 0 for ~70s even though we processed a top-up at reset. Request ids: req_ab12, req_ab13. Can you check?

alice (Support): Sorry about that, Ben. Can you paste org id + the exact observed times? Do you still see 0 in the console or logs?

ben (AcmeCorp): Org: ORG-8923. Observed UI zero at 2026-03-01T00:00:05Z, top-up charge posted at 2026-03-01T00:00:30Z (card charge visible). Streaming clients got 429s starting 00:00:02 and then kept retrying until ~00:01:15 when tokens came back.

alice (Support): Thx. Looping in infra and billing: @dave (SRE) @carmen (Billing) — looks like a refill vs top-up timing/race.

dave (SRE): I’m looking. Can you attach a small snippet of the streaming client logs around the reconnects? Specifically any lines with HTTP 429 or reserve_token errors. Also any socket IDs.

ben (AcmeCorp): Paste of client log (trimmed):
```
[2026-03-01T00:00:01.987Z] socket=so_01 reserve_token -> 429 throttle
[2026-03-01T00:00:03.102Z] reconnecting...
[2026-03-01T00:00:30.455Z] payment_event: card_charged id=pay_9X
[2026-03-01T00:00:45.210Z] socket=so_01 reserve_token -> 429
[2026-03-01T00:01:12.001Z] socket=so_01 reserve_token -> 200 tokens_left=1200
```

dave (SRE): This pattern is exactly what I expect for a transient cache-stale window. TL;DR: our quota service writes new balances at reset, but streaming proxies keep an in-memory quota cache with TTL=60s. If a top-up occurs after reset (like your 00:00:30) and proxies are still serving data from the 60s-cached entry, long-lived sockets will attempt reservations against the stale zero balance and get 429s until cache expires or proxy is invalidated.

carmen (Billing): Confirmed payment/pay_9X cleared at 00:00:30 and we posted the allocation to the account soon after. Billing side did its write at 00:00:30.

alice (Support): So the chain is: reset job sets monthly allotment at 00:00:00 -> customer usage + streaming reservations continue -> top-up at 00:00:30 increases balance -> streaming proxies still hold cached zero until TTL expires (~00:01:00) -> requests get 429s in between.

ben (AcmeCorp): Ok that fits. Any short-term mitigation for us? The dropped sessions caused a live demo to fail.

dave (SRE): Short-term options: 1) restart streaming processes / reopen sockets (new connections fetch fresh balance) — simplest for customers. 2) If you can tolerate a small delay, we can temporarily bump your org's ephemeral emergency credits for 15m so no 429s while we patch. Which would you prefer?

ben (AcmeCorp): Restarting was easiest for us; we restarted and saw tokens appear at ~00:01:10. But the demo took a hit. We’d appreciate the emergency credit for 15m if you can.

carmen (Billing): I’ll issue a 15-minute ephemeral credit of 2k tokens (code: EMERG-8923) now and note it on the invoice.

alice (Support): Filed a follow-up: we’ll do a short-term config change to reduce streaming proxy quota cache TTL from 60s -> 5s during the next maintenance window and add an immediate invalidation hook on billing/topup events. @deploy-bot please schedule a canary rollout.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout scheduled to eng-runtime canary on 2026-03-02T03:00:00Z UTC. Release notes: reduce streaming quota cache TTL; add topup invalidation hook (feature-req #PLAT-421).

dave (SRE): Long-term: we’re implementing event-driven invalidation on the quota event bus so any write (reset, top-up, manual credit) pushes an immediate invalidation to proxies. That will eliminate the transient zero window for long-lived sockets. Plan ETA: 3 weeks.

ben (AcmeCorp): Thanks all. Restart + emergency credit worked, demo recovered. Please confirm when the TTL change is live so we can plan future demos. :thumbsup:

alice (Support): Will update this thread when the canary passes. Closing interim: root cause = cache TTL + ordering of reset vs top-up writes. Permanent fix in progress. :white_check_mark:
